bibliography.author: Andrew Wiles
bibliography.title: The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture
bibliography.locator: Printed p.4, §2 Recent History, unnumbered theorem; p.2 Remark1 separates the refined leading-coefficient formula; p.4 reference[1] records the 2001 modularity theorem.
supports: All elliptic curves over Q are modular; rank equality therefore holds for analytic rank0 or1.
The refined leading-coefficient formula is a separate statement.

mathematicalContract.objects: E is a nonsingular smooth projective genus-one curve over Q with a specified Q-rational identity; equivalently an elliptic curve over Q.
mathematicalContract.lFunction: The Hasse–Weil L(E,s), including the correct bad-prime factors, with its known modular analytic continuation; r_an(E)=ord_{s=1} L(E,s). This is not a finite truncated Euler product.
mathematicalContract.sha: Sha(E/Q)=ker(H^1(Q,E) -> product_v H^1(Q_v,E)), over all places v.
mathematicalContract.quantifiers: For every elliptic curve E/Q, if r_an(E) belongs to {0,1}, then rank_Z E(Q)=r_an(E) and Sha(E/Q) is finite.

modularityDependency.statement: Every elliptic curve over Q is modular.

hypotheses: L(E,1) != 0, with the analytically continued global L-function.

hypotheses: L(E,1)=0 and L′(E,1) != 0, as exact statements about the analytically continued global L-function.

notConcluded: This adapter supplies no formula for the leading coefficient L^(r)(E,1)/r!, the exact order of Sha, regulator, periods or Tamagawa product.
No rank>=2 conclusion or arbitrary-number-field generalization is obtained.
A finite list of local factors, a sampled graph, or |L(E,1)| below a numerical tolerance does not establish either exact analytic-rank hypothesis.

hypothesisEvidenceRequired: An independently justified global analytic-rank0 or1 statement, with source/proof scope retained
